description: A list of people, each row a face with a name and, where the list is about a quantity, a figure beside it. Standings, assignees, members, suggestions. The list owns the semantics and the row size; a row owns what it says.

label.description: Names the list for assistive technology: what these people are a list OF, never that they are people. "Ruby league standings", "Suggested accounts", never "People". Required and guarded at runtime rather than defaulted, because nothing can derive it. A name that only says what the component is satisfies the requirement mechanically and tells a screen-reader user nothing. Two lists on one page announce identically.

ordered.description: Whether the order is part of the meaning. A standings table read in any other order is a different claim, and its rows are numbered; a set of suggestions is a set. The order is a declared input rather than something inferred from the rows carrying a `rank`, because Arena never derives what it draws from what a consumer happened to pass. A numbered list whose numbers are decoration is a lie told to a screen reader.

content.description: The rows. One ArenaPersonRow per person; a row is what says who and how much, and the list decides only where each one goes.
